memory_lessons.applicability: Warp-local transpose tuning; a smaller subgroup is a useful contrast, not an assumed improvement.
memory_lessons.claim: The selected 16×16-subgroup program measured 3.382080079366667e-6 seconds, slightly faster than the 8×8-subgroup program at 3.4255999295666667e-6 seconds; reducing the subgroup further trades fewer values per thread for shorter store segments and more warps.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this four-lane-subgroup variant on the same correctness sizes and repeated n=1024 protocol.

memory_lessons.claim: A full-warp 32×32 ownership variant measured 3.832746607563334e-6 seconds, slower than the selected 16×16-subgroup result; larger ownership per warp is not by itself evidence of a faster transpose.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare alternative ownership sizes using controller timings and available build diagnostics rather than shuffle-count estimates alone.

proposal.hypothesis: A warp can load a 4×32 input strip with adjacent lanes reading adjacent columns, then transpose four-lane subtiles by exchanging the two low lane bits with two register-index bits using only width-4, same-warp shuffles. This reduces values and shuffle stages per thread compared with the selected 16×16-subgroup parent, but requires eight warps per 32×32 tile and writes in four-float segments, so the store transactions or added warps may outweigh the reduced per-thread work.

retained: Changed ownership to eight warps per 32×32 tile, with each warp loading a 4×32 strip and each lane holding four input-row values for one column.
Transposed 4×4 subtiles by swapping two register-index bits and two low lane bits through width-4 warp-local XOR shuffles; no cross-warp shuffle, shared-memory staging, or CTA barrier is used.
Stored bit-preserved unsigned float representations to output using size_t offsets; retained the run entry point and 32×32 grid coverage for positive n divisible by 32.
